message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you decide). Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes “Uno.” | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (red, yellow, green, blue) × 25 cards each (numbers 0‑9 + two of each action card). 4 Wild and 4 Wild Draw Four cards. | | **Setup** | Shuffle the deck. Deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn order** | Clockwise (unless a reverse card changes direction). | | **Playing a card** | On your turn, play one card that matches either the color or the value of the top discard. If you have no playable card, you must draw from the draw pile. | | **Action cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – changes direction of play.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and skips a turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and skips a turn (must be played only if you have no matching color). | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you’re down to one card, shout “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a round** | The first player to get rid of all their cards wins the round. | | **Scoring** | Add up the point values of the cards left in each opponent’s hand:
• Number cards = face value.
• Skip/Reverse/Draw Two = 20 points.
• Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50 points.
The winner of the round gets those points added to their total. | | **Game end** | First player to reach 500 points (or a pre‑agreed target) wins the game. | **Optional house rules** - *Stacking*: Allow players to stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards instead of drawing immediately. - *No “draw four” rule*: Some groups forbid playing Wild Draw Four unless you truly have no other playable card. - *“Uno” penalty*: Instead of drawing two cards, the player who forgot to call Uno may lose a turn. Enjoy!
